fullPassage:
It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc.

(A) If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
(B) One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison.
(C) We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us. But it doesn't always work this way.

They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman — and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us. But it doesn't always work this way.

For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up. One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem ②<u>unapproachable</u>, distant, superhuman — and make us ③<u>look bad</u> (and feel worse) by comparison. We have a better chance of doing well in our own life tasks when around someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to ④<u>teach</u> us. But it doesn't always work this way.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: those who are too competent — 보어 자리에 형용사 competent가 필요. 명사 competence는 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① competence — 원문은 competent(형용사). be동사 뒤 보어 자리에 명사 competence가 오면 'too competence'가 되어 부적절 ←정답
❌ ② unapproachable — 형용사 보어로 적절 (seem unapproachable)
❌ ③ look bad — 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 원형동사 구조로 적절
❌ ④ teach — to부정사로 적절 (a lot to teach us)
det.tip: those who are too competent — 형용사 보어. competence(명사)는 오류

det.korean: comparison=비교. 비교에 의해 나쁘게 보이고 더 나쁘게 느껴진다

det.korean: someone who knows what they're doing and has a lot to teach us=자기가 하는 일을 알고 우리에게 가르칠 것이 많은 누군가
det.analysis: someone(선행사) + who(관계대명사) + knows(동사1) + what they're doing(명사절) + and(접속사) + has a lot to teach us(동사2 + to부정사). 관계대명사절 + 명사절 + 병렬 구조

questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 유능한 사람을 좋아하지만, 너무 유능하면 불편하고, 실수를 보면 다시 좋아진다는 역설
det.analysis:
✅ ① 유능한 사람에 대한 호감(like)과 불편함(uncomfortable)의 공존, 그리고 실수(fallibility)가 이를 해소한다는 역설적 관계가 글의 주제 ←정답
❌ ② 자기 개발은 언급되지 않음
❌ ③ 비교는 부정적 효과(look bad)로 서술됨
❌ ④ 유능함의 정의는 서두 일부일 뿐 전체 주제가 아님
det.tip: 유능함 → 호감 but 너무 유능함 → 불편함 → 실수 → 호감 회복 = 역설

ch: 유능한 사람에 대한 호감과 불편함의 역설

questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 유능한 사람의 가끔의 실수가 오히려 호감을 높인다는 것이 글의 요지
det.analysis:

❌ ③ '자주 하는 사람'이 아니라 '가끔(every once in a while)' 하는 것이 핵심

det.tip: evidence of fallibility → like better — 실수의 증거가 호감을 높인다
